79617.subject: 4 Ways To Protect Your Career From AI Disruption
79617.body:
Forbes Edge

Автор: Forbes


Автор: Forbes

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/4-ways-protect-your-career-from-ai-disruption-forbes-magazine-awmec?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BpWtCcPAERWefs1ovVj3EVw%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=0nxfazN4jSgYs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mue84zk6~i6-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mue84zk6-i6
  
Amid a changing employment landscape, 76% of millennial workers, currently ages 30 to 45, are actively questioning their career paths, according to Glassdoor data. Additionally, 68% say they’ve delayed a major life milestone due to career uncertainty.  This is a generation that should be familiar with disruption, since many came of age during the Great Recession and weathered mass layoffs during the global pandemic. But Chris Martin, Glassdoor’s senior economist, explains that today’s layoffs and AI disruption are even more disconcerting for millennials since they’re happening at a pivotal point in their careers. As a result, he says many millennials are taking a proactive approach to building a broader, more diversified professional foundation, which Glassdoor refers to as “stability stacking.” “Millennials are at the point in their career now where they should be the most stable,” Martin says. “They’ve reached management, an increasing number are approaching leadership positions where they’re in the C-Suite or VP or above. They’re reaching peak earnings as well. So there are all these things that are the hallmarks of a solid mid-career, but that’s just not what millennials are feeling.” I spoke to Martin, as well as millennial executive coach Janel Abrahami, about how millennials—as well as professionals of any generation—can “stability stack” their career to build some level of security in today’s market. Here’s a glimpse of what they had to say: Build your network: While creating a new side hustle may seem like an obvious step to stability stacking, Abrahami encourages professionals to not underestimate the impact of building opportune connections. “Maybe neither of you are sure on how you’ll work together in the beginning, but you kind of just know that you will,” she says. “And when that opportunity arises, at least you have that person on speed dial should you need to tap into them.” Stack your skills: With so much uncertainty around AI and how it will reshape certain roles, Martin says taking a skills-based approach to stability stacking could be a smart move. “Think about a couple of different skill-based responses where you can gain proficiency in AI-based skills or skills that are more resilient to AI replacement,” he suggests. This includes human skills such as effective communication, storytelling and adaptability.  Share your expertise
